title: Learning by ear and making up blues
summary: Pete had no teacher, makes blues from sounds in the air, and can make one on any subject.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Did you have a teacher for music?

No, I didn't. I just like myself. All music that I play, I just play by air, you know, just air music, you know. Well, I may be walking along, riding on the car, and the blues come to me. When they come to me, and I just get it all in my head, well, I come back and I get my guitar and I play it.
Well, what are these blues about that you sing?

Well, just like anything else, you know, that follows you, you know. Say, if I had an automobile and I said I wanted to go to town, I'd go and get in my car and I'd go in on the town and get it off my mind, you know. But, just like those blues were, anything that you can hear in the air, music. You'd hear the sound of it, like, coming so far. Oh, it sounds good. I'm going to get my guitar and pick it up and I play it.
You could sit down and make up a blues about any subject if you had to?
Any subject I could sit down and make up a blues.
Well, we'll try it later on.
When Augusta gets back. Yeah. And we'll just name a subject and you can show people how you do it. Yeah. Because you already did that once with that, some got six months.
Well, all of my blues that I put out, I just made up, made of blues. All of my blues made up. I make up my own blues, you see. Yes.
